title: Fabrication of Pulsatile Polymeric Microparticles Encapsulating Rabies Antigen
protocol: Design microparticle structures using a computer-aided design (CAD) program.
Export the final design as an STL file.
Upload the STL file to software capable of defining print parameters.
Save the file as one compatible with the 3D printer.
Pre-treat a silicon printing substrate using a plasma cleaning process.
Immerse the pre-treated substrate into a solution of ethanol and 3-(trimethoxysilyl) propyl methacrylate.
Cover the Petri dish with aluminum foil.
Incubate overnight.
Upload the print file to the multi-photon 3D printer.
Apply the print resin to the treated substrate.
Load the 10x lens.
Print the microstructures.
Submerge the print in propylene glycol methyl ether acetate for 45 min.
Submerge the print in isopropyl alcohol for 5 min.
Post-cure the master mold by exposing it to UV light at 254 nm for 120 min.
Treat the surface of the 3D-printed master mold with Trichloro(1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl) silane in a vacuum chamber.
Pull the vacuum for 1 h at -20 in.Hg relative pressure.
Thoroughly mix the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) prepolymer base with the PDMS prepolymer curing agent in a 9:1 ratio by mass.
Transfer the uncured PDMS to a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 3 min at room temperature.
Place the master mold in an aluminum foil dish.
Pour uncured PDMS on top of the mold to ensure features are submerged.
Place the aluminum foil dish in a vacuum chamber and pull the vacuum at -20 in.Hg for 1 hour.
Remove the aluminum foil dish from the vacuum chamber.
Place 800 µm spacers at the ends of the master mold.
Overlay a clean glass slide onto the master mold to avoid introducing air bubbles.
Clamp the mold and slide together with binder clips over the spacers.
Cure the prepolymer into PDMS molds in an oven set to 120 °C for at least 4 hours.
Remove the structure from the oven after curing.
Release the binder clips carefully.
Separate the master mold from the cured PDMS mold using a razor blade.
Place the c-clamped assembly in a vacuum oven set to 120 °C for 30 min under vacuum with a relative pressure of -30 in.Hg.
Remove the assembly from the oven and firmly tighten the clamp.
Return the tightened assembly to the vacuum oven for another 30 min.
Remove the assembly from the oven and allow it to cool for 4 h in a desiccator.
Once cooled, loosen the clamp.
Remove the PLGA film from the nonstick polymer sheets using tweezers or a scalpel.
Place the PLGA film in a labeled Petri dish.
Store the Petri dish inside a desiccator for later use.
Treat the surface of the PDMS mold as described previously.
Cut out and place a portion of the 250 µm PLGA film on the treated PDMS mold using tweezers or a scalpel.
Overlay a clean glass microscope slide over the PLGA film and PDMS mold.
Clamp the components together with a spring clamp directly over the array and PLGA film.
Place the clamped mold assembly in the vacuum oven set to 120 °C, pull the vacuum with a relative pressure of -30 in.Hg for 1 h.
Remove the clamped mold assembly from the oven and let it cool passively at room temperature for approximately 15 min.
Using a razor blade, gently apply pressure between the PDMS mold and PLGA particle array to separate the two.
Store the PLGA particles in a desiccator for future use.
Thaw one aliquot of commercially available RABV antigen at room temperature.
Place two centrifugal spin filters with a 100 kDa molecular weight cutoff into two collection tubes.
Prewet the two centrifugal spin filters by adding 500 µL of UltraPure water and spinning at 2,400 x g for 1 min in a benchtop centrifuge at room temperature.
Remove the water from both the top and bottom compartments of the filtration setup using a 200 µL pipette.
Add 400 µL of distilled water to the top compartment of each spin filter, then add 100 µL of the thawed RABV antigen and mix with the pipette.
Load the two centrifugal spin filters into a benchtop centrifuge, ensuring that the filters face the center of the centrifuge.
Centrifuge the filters at 14,000 x g for 10 min at room temperature.
Retrieve the filters from the centrifuge.
Remove the filtrate in the collection tubes using a pipette and discard.
Add 450 µL of filtered distilled water to each filter.
Mix the concentrated sample and water by pipetting up and down six times.
Centrifuge the two spin filters at 14,000 x g for 10 min at room temperature.
Remove the filtrate from each tube using a pipette and discard.
Remove the spin filters from the collection tubes.
Cap the filter casings using the top of the collection tubes.
Place the bottom of the spin filter casings directly onto a vortex.
Vortex at 3,000 rpm for 30 s while holding the filter casings upright and at 45° angles.
Carefully remove the cap of the collection tubes from the spin filter casings.
Place the filter casings back in the provided collection tubes.
Run a quick spin (2-3 s) to collect any volume that may have become trapped in the cap.
Vacuum filter 500 mL of deionized water through a 0.22 µm vacuum filter.
Degas the filtered solution by applying a vacuum (relative pressure: -20 in.Hg) while under sonication for 20 min.
Attach piezo dispense capillaries to the piezoelectric dispenser.
Prime the machine according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Place the slide with PLGA particles into the dispensing area.
Set up the "Find Target Reference Points".
Run the setup process.
Set up the "Target Substrate".
Load 25 µL of concentrated antigen into the source plate.
Load the source plate into the machine.
Aspirate 10 µL of concentrated antigen into the dispensing tip using PDCs.
Wash the outside of the dispensing tip.
Calibrate the dispensing alignment.
Enter "Target Setup parameters".
Click on Run to begin particle loading.
Verify that filled particles are correctly loaded under a stereoscope.
Place a stainless-steel block on a hotplate.
Place two microscope slides on the stainless-steel block parallel to each other.
Ensure the stainless-steel block is level.
Turn the hotplate on and set the temperature so that the surface reaches 200 °C.
Verify the temperature of the hotplate before sealing.
Suspend filled PLGA particles above a hotplate by placing them on two glass slides.
Start a timer for 18 seconds.
Remove the particle array from the hotplate once sealed and suspend it over the lab bench using two separate glass slides.
Allow the particles to cool for 1 minute.

Harvest the cooled particles using a scalpel while looking through a stereoscope, holding the scalpel at a 45° angle to the slide and applying pressure to the base of the particle to separate it from the glass slide.
Transfer harvested particles into 0.5 mL low-protein binding tubes.
Fill the tubes with 250 μL of a 1x phosphate buffer solution (PBS) containing 30 mg/mL bovine serum albumin (BSA) and 1 mg/mL glucose.
Crush particles under a stereoscope using fine-tip tweezers.
Store samples at 4°C until antigen potency can be evaluated by ELISA within 7 days.
Prepare buffers as instructed in Supplementary File 1.
Mix 25 µL of coating antibody with 4975 µL of carbonate-bicarbonate buffer (pH 9.6) to prepare the coating solution.
Dispense 50 µL of coating solution into each well of a microplate using a multichannel pipette.
Tap the plate edges gently on a gloved palm to ensure even coverage at the bottom of each well.
Seal the plate with adhesive film and place it at 37°C for 1 hour.
Transfer plates to 4°C overnight.
Retrieve plates from cold storage and wash wells three times with 200 µL of wash buffer each.
Remove the wash buffer from each well.
Dispense 300 µL of blocking buffer into each well.
Proceed plate-by-plate when running multiple plates with repeated samples.
Do not apply material to all plates before moving on to the next type of material to avoid wells drying out.
After the final wash step, keep wash buffer in the wells until immediately before adding samples.
Cover unused wells of the ELISA plate with a plastic 96-well plate lid.
Move the lid sequentially to reveal additional wells as they are dispensed into.
Seal the plates with adhesive plastic film.
Incubate the sealed plates at 37 ± 2 °C for 60 ± 5 min.
Prepare the standard curve and test samples during this incubation.
Predilute the antigen being evaluated in diluent buffer at a recommended dilution of 0.125 IU/mL.
Ensure an excess volume of at least 40 µL to account for pipetting loss.
Evaluate all samples in duplicate on each ELISA plate.
Include a twofold dilution series for eight points in columns 2 and 3 of each ELISA plate.
Perform a twofold dilution series of each sample along the columns of the plate in low-bind protein 96-well plates or tubes.
Load the start of the dilution series in row A with double the final volume required.
Load 120 μL of diluent buffer into all wells on the low-bind protein plate except columns 1 and 12 (i.e., B2 through H11).
Transfer 120 µL of sample from A2-A11 to B2-B11 using a multichannel pipette.
Mix well by pipetting up and down several times in B2-B11 while avoiding splashing and bubbles.
Repeat the transfer process, moving down the plate along the columns until wells H2-H11 are reached.
Discard the remaining 120 µL volume aspirated from the final row of wells.
Transfer 100 µL of diluent buffer into columns 1 and 12 as the "blanks" using a multichannel pipette.
Transfer 100 µL from each well of the low-bind protein 96-well plate containing sample dilutions to the washed ELISA plate using a multichannel pipette.
Repeat for all ELISA plates being run.
Seal the plates with an adhesive plastic film.
Place the sealed plates in an incubator for 60 ± 5 min at 37 ± 2 °C.
Prepare the detection antibody solution by adding 4.4 µL of the antibody solution to 10,995.6 µL of diluent buffer.
Mix well by pipetting up and down several times.
Mix 11 mL of solution immediately before use for ELISA analysis, accounting for pipetting losses.
Wash the plates five times with 200 μL of wash buffer.
Aspirate remaining wash buffer from each well.
Dispense 100 μL of detection antibody solution into each well using a multichannel pipette.
Seal the microplate with adhesive plastic film.
Incubate the sealed plate at 37 ± 2 °C for 60 ± 5 minutes.
Prepare conjugate by mixing 4.4 µL of streptavidin-peroxidase conjugate solution with 10,995.6 µL of wash buffer immediately before use.
Wash plates five times with 200 μL of wash buffer after detection antibody incubation.
Aspirate remaining wash buffer from each well.
Dispense 100 μL of the conjugate solution to each well using a multichannel pipette.
Seal the microplate again with adhesive plastic film.
Incubate the sealed plate at 37 ± 2 °C for 60 ± 5 minutes.
Prepare the substrate during the final wash step according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Dissolve one tablet of o-phenylenediamine dihydrochloride (OPD) in 9 mL of deionized water in the dark.
Top up with 1 mL of 10x stable peroxide buffer.
Wash the plates five times with 200 µL of wash buffer.
Dispense 100 µL of substrate to each well using a multichannel pipette.
Seal the plates with an adhesive plastic film.
Leave the plates on the bench for 10-20 min, protected from light, using aluminum foil.
Monitor color development visually to avoid saturation.
Add 50 µL of stop solution to each well.
Read the plate immediately for absorbance at 492 nm and a reference absorbance of 620 nm.
Analyze the data using the corrected absorbance reading (reading at 492 nm minus the reading at 620 nm).
Subtract the average of the blank from all samples.
Use a sigmoidal 4PL interpolation method to convert absorbance values to IU/mL.
Multiply by the total sample volume (250 µL) to convert to IU.
